data.raw_text:
This system exists for a simple reason:
pilots—like people—sometimes get too close without meaning to.

Meet TCAS: the Traffic Collision Avoidance System.
Or, as pilots know it:
the calm voice that politely informs you someone is very much in your personal space.

🟢 Green Zone — Surveillance
Factual: TCAS detects traffic miles away. No action needed.
Relatable: You notice someone across the room. You register their existence. You act unbothered. All is well.

🟡 Yellow Zone — Traffic Advisory (TA)
Factual: “Traffic, traffic.” Another aircraft is getting closer.
Relatable: Your friend leans in and whispers, “Hey… that person keeps looking at you.”
No panic. Just awareness. For now.

🔴 Red Zone — Resolution Advisory (RA)
Factual: TCAS issues vertical commands: “Climb” or “Descend.” You comply immediately.
Relatable: Someone texts, “We need to talk.”
No discussion. No hesitation. You move. Now.

The rule pilots live by:
• ATC can be wrong
• Your instincts can be wrong
• TCAS does not care about feelings

If it says climb — you climb.
If it says descend — you descend.
Hesitate, and things get uncomfortable very fast.

TCAS works because it accepts one universal truth:
two intelligent beings can still end up in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Same with dating.
Same with marriage.
Same with family group chats.

The difference?
TCAS gives clear instructions.
Life usually lets you figure it out… mid-air. ✈️

data.raw_text:
TCAS is basically aviation’s social awareness system — except it has absolutely no manners.

Here’s what those symbols really mean in real life:

🔹 Other Traffic (Blue Diamond)
Factual: Aircraft detected. No immediate threat.
Relatable: Someone else is in the room. You noticed. You moved on with your life.

🔷 Proximate Traffic (Filled Blue Diamond)
Factual: Traffic is getting closer, laterally or vertically.
Relatable: Someone’s standing a little too close while talking. Still okay… but you subtly shift away.

🟡 Traffic Advisory – TA (Yellow Circle)
Factual: TCAS says, “Pay attention,” but doesn’t tell you what to do.
Relatable: Your partner says, “I’m not mad. I just want to talk.”
You’re alert. You’re listening. Your stress level just doubled.

🔴 Resolution Advisory – RA (Red Square)
Factual: TCAS issues a vertical command that must be followed immediately.
Relatable: The moment in life when discussion is officially over.
You do exactly what you’re told — now. No questions. No debate.

Pilots don’t panic when TCAS speaks.
We comply — like adults who’ve learned that arguing never improves the outcome.
